EventName: Throat Punch Thursday - Summer MTB Short Track (XCC) Race Series
EventNotes:
Throat Punch Thursday 

MTB Short Track (XCC) Training Races
Summer Series
 


Powered by RVA Racing | USAC Sanctioned | National Points Qualifier

REGISTRATION CLOSES AT 1:00 PM TODAY


Race Nights

August 13 • August 20 • August 27
Heats start at 6:00 PM sharp. Know your category start time. Don’t roll up late unless you like watching from the sidelines.

Dogwood Dell - Barker Field: 1300 Blanton Ave, Richmond, VA 23221 (Google Maps)


The Rules - Pay Attention.

  • MTBs only!
  • This is USA Cycling Sanctioned MTB Race - USAC XCC format and rules apply.
  • Keep your Bib Plate. Bib plates are issued for the series.
  • Check in. Starts at 5:30. ALL racers MUST check in before each race – each day.
  • Registration closes at NOON on race day
  • NO WALK-ON REGISTRATIONS  


START TIMES

  • 6:00 PM - Fight Club
    • Intermediate Men & Boys (7-laps)
    • Beginner Men & Boys (5-laps)
    • Beginner Women & Girls (5-laps)  
  • 6:30 PM – Bareknuckle Brawlers
    • Expert Men & Boys (9-laps)
    • Masters Men & Women (7-laps)
    • Expert Women & Girls (9-laps)
    • Intermediate Women & Girls (7-laps)
  • 7:00 PM - The THROAT PUNCH
    • Rolling Start. 2-laps. All Out. No Hiding.
    • Open Men & Women / Boys & Girls (2-laps)


Race Format:

  • The TPT races are held on a course of .50 - .65 miles in lap distance with 60 - 75 feet of elevation gain each lap.
  • Lap counts are estimated based on first lap time.
  • Podiums based on most laps, lowest time.
  • Riders will cover around 4-10 laps during the 17-22-minute duration of their heat.
  • USAC points are scored for EACH race. 


The Course.

  • We are NOT racing on the Dogwood trails.
  • Each week's course is a custom, hand-built track right by the pavilion next to Barker Field.
  • This course is VERY spectator friendly - bring the crew and your best heckle game.
  • And yes - it changes every week to keep it spicy. Stay sharp.


Course Drops.

  • We design each course the week of the race.
  • Registered racers will receive course drops via email.


The Vibe:

Expect elbows-out racing. Bring your lungs, bring your legs, and maybe bring an ice pack for that ego (short track has a way of finding you).

It’s fast. It’s ridiculous. It’s fun.
  

USAC Sanctioning and Points:

  • ONLY USAC annual license holders will receive points!
  • Annual license holders ranked in order of finish for reporting.
  • Forget to enter your USAC ID at registration = NO POINTS.
  • ALL 3 races are USAC XCC qualifying opportunities for Nationals.
  • ALL 3 races allow you to earn USAC points for XCC Nationals.


Timing.

The TPT is electronically timed. Your bib plate is your RFID timing chip and should be mounted securely to your bars (top of plate) and the bottom of the plate should be mounted to cables, or in a way that makes the number clearly visible from the front of the bike. 

If you bend the plate, try to make it aero, don’t have it secured properly, or alter it in any way, we will NOT get a read. And that will mean all your hard work was for nuthin’ – so please don’t. Come find us if you have any questions on race day. Well also be checking on you.


Other.

Volunteers - We REALLY need volunteers to make this event happen and start on time.

  • 4:30 PM (or sooner): we start marking the course
  • 7:20 PM: course teardown
  • Please email dennis@rvaracing.com if you can help or show up on race day.


RVA Racing brings you bike racing, built by bike racers - We're grassroots, but professionally savage.

We are proud to present the Rocky Hill CX Series as a centralized location for our youth teams to practice at (5:00 PM), and a fun, no-pressure, training race for those looking to enjoy cyclocross racing (5:35 PM for the Juniors and 6:15 PM Open Race). Thanks to the Town of Rocky Hill Parks and Rec and our partner clubs for allowing this to happen!

Volunteers are needed to make this event successful. Sign up to volunteer and you will receive reimbursement on your entry fee. CLICK HERE TO HELP OUT

Series Dates:
This 4-week training series will take place on 4 Wednesdays in August/September. August 26th, Sept 2nd, Sept 9th, and Sept 16th. With respect to the Town of Rocky Hill and their beautiful park, we will cancel due to rain and wet conditions that will be especially damaging to the venue. In this case, we will provide a credit to all participants and you will be notified of a cancelation via email!

A fun, safe and positive weekly Junior Practice Session
This practice is hosted by CCAP staff and regional team coaches. Licensed junior riders under 18 and middle/high schoolers can enjoy a no-pressure practice session at 5:00 PM. Any junior that wants to ride must be at least 9 years old (cyclocross racing age = age on Dec 31st of the 2026 year) and are welcome to race in the Junior Race. All training activities and races will be started with instruction from CCAP coaches and staff. All youth riders, 18 and under, are welcome to participate in the practice for $10. Riders that are on CCAP registered teams may participate in the practice at no charge.

Fun, safe and competitive racing for all
Fun, friendly, and competitive racing for everyone from novice racers to experienced Category 1 Racers. The wide variety of skill levels makes for an informal, no-pressure vibe. 

All riders must have a USA Cycling License. If you don't have one, one-day beginner licenses may be purchased for $15 and are valid for a single day. One-day beginner licenses may only be purchased by new riders or Category 5 riders.

Equipment
All USAC Rules apply. All riders must wear a helmet. A cyclocross bike or mountain bike (without bar-ends) is suggested. No BMX bikes allowed.

New to cyclocross?
Check out THIS VIDEO to learn what it's all about!

For full information about our weekly race series, we encourage you to visit our website: https://catamountoutdoor.org/race-series-weekly/

 

In the event that the race is cancelled for inclement weather, your entry can be transferred to a different week.

 

A huge thank you to our 2026 series sponsors!

World famous Wednesday Worlds cyclocross practice at Holster Park, in Clifton NJ. Come build skills and fitness for the cyclocross racing season. 

Wheels down 5:30 - we will do a mix of skills and drills to build fitness before moving on to hot lap and race pace efforts. Session ends around 730 depending on weather, daylight and conditions.  Meet at the tennis courts.  

Location:  https://www.google.com/maps/place/Holster+Park/@40.8593319,-74.188589,16z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x89c2ffb3b0eb8ab1:0xa15abc2860c1a7ec!8m2!3d40.8593319!4d-74.1860141!16s%2Fg%2F1tdwr0j4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MDgyOC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D

  • Park on the road between the school and the baseball field. Do NOT park in the fenced area behind the school.  
  • Event may be cancelled due to weather.  Check your email and join the Facebook Group for the latest info.
  • Be nice to each other.

EventNotes:
ON-LINE REGISTRATION ONLY … VIA BIKEREG

Race-Day Schedule: 

  • 2:30pm - Deadline for any weather related notices (to be shared via bikereg email list)
  • 4:45pm to 5:30pm - Racer Sign-In at the NHMS Front Gate w/NHMS Staff & SRT Staff.  All racers must pay a $10 gate fee to NHMS at sign-in each week, spectators pay $5.
  • 5:15pm - NHMS infield opens and warm-up begins
  • 6:00pm - Racing begins

Race Dates - Planned Courses (subject to change): 

  • 4/16 – Magic Mile
  • 4/23 – TBA
  • 4/30 – Road Course
  • 5/07 – Magic Mile or Frontier
  • 5/14 – Road Course
  • 5/21 – Road Course

Categories and Numbers:  There are three fields for the series:  A, B, and C. You will indicate your field of choice by answering a custom question during registration.

The A field is intended primarily for riders in Category 3 or above.  Category 5 racers should not register for the A field except with prior permission from the race promoter (send email to sunapeeracing@gmail.com), or inquire at the gate during registration.  The B field is recommended for experienced riders with considerable strength.  The C field is recommended for all other riders, including new and slower riders.  If you register for a field and decide you want to make a change before the race, please let us know at the gate.

Junior Membership:  Available to persons 17 years of age or younger.  A parent or guardian will need to be in attendance to sign the waivers for the race and entry into the NHMS facility.  If you are unable to accompany the minor, please make prior arrangements with the race director to ensure that all necessary forms are completed in advance.

NHMS Gate Entry Fee:  The series pass does not include the NHMS gate entry.  The gate entry fee is $10 per adult racer, or $5 for juniors and spectators.  The gate fee is paid directly to NHMS at gate, and helps cover costs of ambulance, personnel and other direct costs associated with hosting the race at their venue. Please Note: Failure to pay the gate fee will result in a permanent ban from participating in the NHMS series. 

Weather Cancellations:  We try hard to avoid cancelling races due to weather, but sometimes mother nature happens.  We will send out cancellation notices by email to all Bikereg registrants.

New Racers:  New racers are always welcome.  If you are a new racer and/or it is your first time at the series, please feel free to contact the race director with any questions or ask for assistance during registration.  The race series is a welcoming environment, and there are many experienced racers at the series who are happy to assist new racers. 

The Courses:  The races are run on four courses:  (1) the road; (2) the inner road; (3) frontier; and (4) the magic mile.  We will attempt to notify racers which course will be used in advance, but do not have control over last minute changes.  For information about the various courses, please see the photographs and information at the bottom of this registration page.

Season Passes:  Season passes are available on bikereg.com: https://www.bikereg.com/nhms

Licenses and Rules:  A USA Cycling license is NOT required for a series pass and/or day-of registration.  All USA Cycling Rules for helmets apply.  No Aero Bars.  Please visit the NHMS page on our website for rules about the series.

The Potential Race Courses:

1.  The Road Course is a 1.5 miles course at NHMS that is used for motorcycle races.  There are two short big ring hills included in this course.  The race length is based on available daylight and will likley be 18 laps (July and August) and 15 laps (September).  Check out Strava for details:  https://www.strava.com/segments/619600

 

2.  The Oval Course is a .9 mile pancake flat course with no elevation gain.  It is typically run with one of the chicanes.  The use of chicanes will be announced at the beginning of the oval race.  Generally a 30 lap race depending on daylight. Length will be announced before the race.  Check out Strava for details:  https://www.strava.com/segments/733975

 

3.  The Frontier Course is a 1 mile course in the back stretch of the NHMS grounds, and includes a moderately technical corner leading into a short incline.  A great course for building power and working on technical skills.  Generally a 24 lap race.  Length will be announced before the race.  Here is the segment on Strava:  http://www.strava.com/segments/619597

4.  The Magic Mile Course was created in 2017 and received rave reviews, and we have now incorporated the Magic Mile course in our rotation.  This is a 1 mile course that races like a fun crit.  Here is the segment on Strava:  https://www.strava.com/segments/15840249

Welcome to the first annual Interlude 360 mile ultra bike race! 

22+ miles of single track - 92 miles of pavement - 246+ miles of gravel and B roads

Start Location - Red Wheel Bike shop - 400 West Main Street Jefferson City, Missouri 65101

Starting time - 0900 - Friday - September 4th 2026  (Registration Sign in will begin at 08:00 am)

Rules

Every year the rules can change. The fastest participant is usually the one that knows the rules.

This is not a closed course you are responsible for your person and all belongings you take or acquire along the way. You will have to carry your bike at some time. You could definitely get your feet wet. everyone and any one that may be affiliated with Red wheel Bike shop and Interlude bike race is not held liable for any of your actions before, during, or after this event.

Drafting is allowed

No littering

Every Participant must utilize a front and rear light at night.

If you go off course you must reenter at the same place. 

You can secure a sleeping arrangement before the begins.

Everyone is allowed to have support during the event. This means food, water and even utilizing a vehicle to sleep in. Hopefully this will allow beginner and new ultra cyclists to  test their abilities before jumping into a even bigger event.

Don't be a dick!

Allowed - 

  • Aero bars
  • Super Tuck
  • Super Aero helmets
  • Any width of handlebars
  • Drop bar mountain bikes
  • Any sock height

Race route - The route will start at Jefferson City and move north to Macon, Missouri and circle back.

This is the unofficial route.

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55489174

*August 1st the race route will be posted on the internet and e-mailed to all participants. 

Popular Questions: 

Will there be aid stations? No you will need to bring or purchase every thing you need to survive.

What type of bike will I need? That is up to you! As race director, I believe a gravel bike with a minimum of 45mm tires will be needed. I would not recommend a road bike. Any mountain bike would work.

Is there a cut off time to finish?  No  - If you take longer than 72 hours you will be considered a finisher but no one will be at the finish line to meet you. 

Will there be SAG if I can't finish? Yes, If you need help getting back to the finish line for any uncertain reason a SAG driver will be of assistance. Please understand you could be waiting a while if you are at the other end of the course. Once you decide you can not finish the course you are considered DNF. You are able to have help from any friends, team or family. 

Where can I sleep on the course? Sleeping is always an option. Motels, AIRBB, VRBO, AND campsites are preferred. If you decide to sleep any where else know the law. Don't Trespass. Stay out of ditches. Be aware of your surroundings. You are welcome to sleep in a sag drivers vehicle. 

Can I ride without a Spot Tracker? No, The Spot Tracker is not only for friends and family to follow you but also for safety.

All participants will be required to wear a bicycle helmet at all times while riding. Penalty is DQ.

Outside (non racer) assistance is only permitted in the pit area. Non racers may not assist out on the course. Racers may assist other racers and are encouraged to do so.

All food and drink for the race must be either carried with the racer or staged in the pit area. There will be 1 water stop on the course as well.

Due to the number of racers on the trail, earbuds are prohibited.

Race numbers must be visible at all times and must be mounted to the handlebars on the front of the bike.

Littering is not permitted. First offense is 15 minute penalty, 2nd offense is DQ.

Cutting the course is not permitted. Penalty is DQ and public ridicule.

In the event of an unfixable mechanical, the racer must complete the lap along the entire course with his/her bike to receive credit for the lap. You MAY back track or shortcut back to the pit to fix your bike, but you will not receive credit for that lap. Do not enter the timing/exchange area if you are coming back from an incomplete lap. Please be honest.

Please exercise caution and good sportsmanship when passing other racers on the trail. Announce your intention to pass rather than just forcing your way by with no warning. Most riders will gladly let you pass.

Solos need to complete one lap to be considered official finishers. Teams need each person to complete at least one lap to be considered official finishers.

Once you reach your pit, you may change any equipment you want, including bikes, and you may stay there as long as you'd like.

WINNERS WILL BE DETERMINED BY NUMBER OF LAPS COMPLETED IN THE GIVEN TIME. IF MULTIPLE RIDERS HAVE THE SAME NUMBER OF LAPS THEN LAP TIMES WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE WINNER!

Down for Gravel is a gravel cycling event that brings riders together for a challenging and rewarding day on the backroads of western Maine. The start and finish are situated on the picturesque Mirror Lake, providing a scenic backdrop for the day’s ride. Routes wind through forest roads, rolling terrain, and offer stunning views—including glimpses of Mount Washington on clear days. Whether you’re looking to push your limits or enjoy a solid day of riding with great company, this event is all about community and the shared experience of gravel cycling.


 

Riders can choose from multiple route options to match their goals for the day. Each course is designed to provide a mix of smooth gravel, rugged sections, and plenty of climbing. The ride is untimed—this is about the experience, not the results.


 

Sunday Cyclocross & Camping:

The weekend kicks off on Saturday with a gravel ride, trail running race and cyclocross clinics.  Offering fast-paced action and a great opportunity to warm up or spectate before Sunday CX race. Riders are encouraged to camp on-site Friday and Saturday night to soak in the atmosphere, connect with fellow cyclists, and make the most of the weekend. The event setup includes a large open field with plenty of space for camping and parking, creating a festival-like setting leading up to race day.


 

Post-Ride Gathering:

After Down For Gravel on Saturday, stick around to share stories, enjoy wood-fired pizza, and relax with a cold beer from Frost Beer Works. A post-ride swim in Mirror Lake is highly recommended—there’s no better way to cool down after a long day on the bike.


 

Location & Accessibility:

West Newfield is conveniently located about an hour’s drive from Portland, Maine, and less than two hours from Boston, making it an easy weekend getaway for gravel riders from across the region.

Inclement Weather Policy

We strive to produce a full and safe bicycle rally, but sometimes the weather conditions can impact those plans. We encourage all participants to arrive as scheduled on the morning of the ride as weather condition-related decisions will be made shortly before the ride start time of 8 AM. In many instances, weather conditions in one part of the State may not be impacting the event location, or weather conditions may improve in the hours preceding the event, both of which impact the ride start. In the event of light to moderate rain, and in the absence of any lightning, our goal is to proceed with the full event if road conditions are safe and will allow the bike ride to take place. If there is lightning in the area, the event will be placed into a weather hold and can be held for up to one hour. If the lightning has departed the area after one hour, the ride can proceed as planned. If there is still evidence of the potential for lightning in the area, the ride may either be shortened or canceled. The event has a one-hour weather hold time frame because the schedule impacts the safety of the event by such factors as increasing traffic on the routes as the day passes, and law enforcement and medical support schedules.

Due to the nature of bike rides taking place generally in the outdoors, weather conditions can play a large role in the production of the event. Because a significant amount of the funds collected during registration have already been expended by the day of the event, and because each event is uniquely scheduled for its date and location, registration refunds are not possible, and rescheduling the event is not feasible, therefore we have a no refund policy. We encourage all those who are pre-registered to pick up their packets with the t-shirt. T-shirts will not be mailed. Proceeds from registration fees and donations will continue to benefit the HALO fund. Thank you for your understanding of these policies. We appreciate your participation.

New to bike racing?: Hydra Cross is a great event to try out bike racing or cyclocross for the first time. There is a free intro to cyclocross racing clinic at 8:00 am on race day that is taught by local, friendly bike racers. Learn the basics to help you enjoy your race. Beginner races following shortly after -- novice men should sign up for the 9:00 am category 4 and beginner race and novice women should sign up for the 11:00 am women's category 4 and 5 race. Just a note on lingo, brand-new racers and novices start as 'category 5' racers. Since we are a USA Cycling sanctioned race, you will need a license but can purchase one when you register at http://bikereg.com/hydracross for $15. If you have any questions about the clinic or racing, please just shoot us an email at hydracrossrace@gmail.com and we'll respond with what you need. 

Course Description: A fun, fast, twisty course that is primarily flat but has some surprising uphill kickers. After a slightly uphill, wide start from the "Legion Shelf," the course heads towards Holyoke's "Muscle Beach" and the hilly southern end of the park. The course design takes full advantage of the elevation to make riders work–but then also brings rewards with a swooping downhill that cuts back and forth across the hill. We have some stinging off-camber sections that will require your skills, with the most challenging and decisive sector coming at the end of the course (see Youtube videos below for a preview). The course runs the full length of the long, linear park with ample opportunities for spectating, with continuous announcing throughout the race by the voice of NCC Hydra Cross 2025, Jake Kravitz. Mountain and river views abound.

Equipment Recommendation: File treads (if dry) and all-around tires will work well for most riders. The course is a mix of grass, dirt, and some pavement. New to cyclocross? Mountain bikes, in any shape, work fine for getting started racing. Road or touring bikes that allow for 32mm tires also work fine.

Race Atmosphere: Come for the race, stay for the atmosphere. Our beer garden and picnic area are family-friendly. There is a playground, splash pad, and popular skate park as well. Our race is known for its good vibes and community-driven feel. 

The excellent Thai Chili Street Food Hub will be serving food in the American Legion Parking lot at lunch time. As usual, expect the American Legion to be serving up coffee, breakfast items, beer and alcohol throughout the day, in addition to lunch and snack items.

Want to do a second race? Great, the second race is just $15, just register for two races at the same time when you sign up.

¿Eres nuevo en las carreras de bicicleta?: Hydra Cross es un evento excelente para probar correr en bicicleta o hacer ciclocrós por primera vez. Hay una clínica gratuita de introducción a las carrera de ciclocrós a las 8 am el día de la carrera que es impartida por corredores de bicicleta locales y amistosos. Aprende los conceptos básicos para ayudarte a disfrutar de tu carrera. Las carreras para principiantes empiezan poco tiempo después -- los hombres novatos deberían inscribirse para la carrera de principiantes categoría 5 de las 9 am, y las mujeres novatas deberían inscribirse para la carrera categoría 4 y 5 de las 10 am. Si tienes alguna pregunta acerca de la clínica o las carreras, por favor envíanos un correo electrónico a hydracrossrace@gmail.com y te responderemos con la información que necesitas.

Descripción del Recorrido: Un recorrido divertido, rápido y sinuoso que es principalmente plano, pero tiene algunas subidas inesperadas. Después de un comienzo levemente cuesta arriba y amplio desde “Legion Shelf”, el recorrido se dirige hacia “Muscle Beach” en Holyoke y hacia el extremo sur montañoso del parque. El diseño del recorrido aprovecha al máximo la elevación para hacer trabajar a los corredores, pero también trae recompensas con un descenso en picada a través de la colina que acorta las idas y vueltas. Tenemos algunos punzantes sectores off-camber que requerirán de tus habilidades, siendo el sector más decisivo y desafiante el que está al final del recorrido (ver el video de Youtube indicado más abajo para una vista preliminar). El recorrido abarca la longitud completa del largo parque lineal, con amplias oportunidades para los espectadores, con relato continuo durante la carrera por la voz de Hydra Cross, Adam Syzmkowickz. Abundan las vistas a la montaña y al río.

Recomendaciones de Equipamiento: Neumáticos con banda de rodamiento lisa (para terreno seco) y multiuso funcionarán bien para la mayoría de los corredores. El recorrido es una combinación de pasto, tierra y algo de pavimento. ¿Eres nuevo en el ciclocrós? Las bicicletas de montaña, en cualquier estado, funcionan bien para empezar a correr. Las bicicletas de carretera o de turismo que permiten usar neumáticos de 32mm también funcionan bien.

Ambiente de Competición: Ven por la carrera, quédate por el ambiente. Nuestro patio cervecero y zona de picnic son aptos para familias. Hay un patio de juegos, juegos de agua y también un parque para patinetas muy popular. Nuestra carrera es conocida por sus buenas vibras y por la sensación de comunidad.

Low registration fees, a friendly race atmosphere and all profits to charity. Mt. Ascutney is the..

 “People's Hill Climb”!   
 

Join us for an ascent up one of the USA’s most iconic climbs! The race takes place on a scenic state park road that’s completely closed to traffic. Compete head to head against some of the finest hill climbers on the east coast, or challenge yourself to conquer one of the hardest hills in the country. 

Our partner is once again the Ascutney Trails Association non-profit and all proceeds from the event will go to their important work developing trails for public use on Mt. Ascutney.

 

REGISTRATION

  • Juniors (under 18) use the code JUNIOR for a $10 discount
  • No USAC license required
  • All proceeds to charity!

 

FAQ

I'm not sure what my FTP is or which wave to register for? Don't stress it! The waves are just to get groups of riders with similar ability the chance to challenge themselves against each other. Just pick one you think is about right. You can always go in and edit your wave later in Bikereg if you change your mind.

I'm not super interested in head to head, I just want to race against the clock? No problem! We will still have  official timing so you can see your official time and how to you stack up against your age group and/or your previous best.

I'm only a Cat 4 but I smash up hills and want to race in Wave A against the heavy hitters? Go for it! The USAC categories are listed as a guide just to help you find the right level of competition, there are no official Cat restrictions. 

What happens if I decide to change my Wave? You can change your category after registering in Bikereg up until registration closes.

 

RACE DAY SCHEDULE

  • Number pick-up open from 8:45 AM until 10 AM.
  • Course is open to riders from 8:45 - 10:15 AM on race day.
  • Drop bags (with clothes, etc.) can be left at the registration table before 10:10 AM to be transported to the finish line.
  • Snacks and hydration (water and Gatorade) will be provided at the finish.
  • The course will close to all traffic promptly at 10:15am
  • No riders or vehicles will be allowed back down the course until the last rider has finished.
  • First wave starts at 10:30 AM.
  • Awards ceremony will take place at the summit after last racer finishes and results are tallied
  • Going back down:
    • Racers need to arrange their own car rides down from the top of the mountain or ride down.
    • Limited parking at the finish line (top of the mountain).  Carpooling is strongly encouraged for those who want to drive down.
    • You may bicycle down after the race. Use caution when descending, there are some frost heaves.
    • Stop frequently to let your brakes and rims cool! Be especially careful if you have carbon rims. Letting a little air out if your tires before starting the ride down the mountain is recommended.

 

WEATHER

  • If it does happen to rain the race will go on, an extra challenge!
  • If conditions are severe (driving rain, high winds, lightning) we will postpone the start for as long as our vendors can accommodate. We will only cancel the race if the conditions refuse to improve and make the course unsafe to ride.
  • In a worst case scenario where we have to cancel we can all head over to Harpoon brewery and commiserate. We have created a virtual route that mimics the course and will schedule a date for a virtual race if needed!
  • All proceeds are going to the Ascutney Trails Association non-profit, so in the end its all for a great cause.

 

DIRECTIONS / LODGING

  • 1826 Back Mountain Rd, Windsor, VT 05089
  • Free parking is available in the field across from the state park (near the start)
  • Mt. Ascutney State Park requires pets to be on a leash less than 10’ or safely confined at all times. Your pet is expected to have current rabies vaccination. Pick up after your pet.
  • Campsites are available at Mt. Ascutney and Wilgus State Parks.   For more information on camping, visit Vermont State Parks or call the Reservation Call Center at 1-888-409-7579 (Mon–Fri, 9am–4pm).

EventName: Elmore Community Trust 6th Annual Gravel Grinder
EventNotes:
Welcome to the 6th Annual Elmore Community Trust Gravel Grinder. If ya know… ya know, but if not, here is some information for you. The Elmore Community Trust (ECT) is a non-profit organization that was founded to care for places that make Elmore special, and to support businesses, organizations and people that contribute positively to our vibrant rural community. Our first project was the purchase and historic preservation of the iconic “Elmore Store”. The purchase of the store has happened, and we are now on to the preservation part. All proceeds or donations from this event go directly towards those preservation efforts. To learn more about the Elmore Store Project, go to our website at www.elmorecommunitytrust.org.

Now for the ride. As in years past, this ride is not for the faint of heart, nor is it a race! The purpose of the ride is to bring folks together to enjoy community and our surroundings, challenge yourselves physically, meet new friends and help support our goal of preserving the Elmore Store. The event takes place on Saturday September 5th. Day of check in will open at 8:00 and the ride will start at 10:00am. This will take place in the church parking lot at 1081 VT Route 12, and the ride will start and end there. This is an 18+ ride, and You must be pre-registered and check in at registration before and after the ride! This is where you get all the important things like food and drink tickets, t-shirts etc. This is also our only way of knowing who is in attendance, and who has made it back safely. Food, drink, and music galore are planned for your return. This ride is tough. There are no short routes or bailout points, and we LOVE some really challenging “gravel roads”, so consider yourselves warned. This year's ride will be about 37miles and 3,800 in elevation. As in year's past, we love some good gnarly class 4! Many people have asked, so we are bringing back the original “CHUNKY ROUTE” from year 1, but with a few variations. We highly recommend some 40mm tires or wider and some good “all terrain” tread. There will be two aid stations along the route that will have water and snacks to refuel. We will try to have more than enough of both for everyone, but we ask that you come prepared to ride as if it were a self-supported ride. We will also try to have a few bare essentials for bike repair on hand at said aid stations. The course will be marked by white signs with big blue arrows on them, and we will have a ride with gps link available for you also. I recommend that you get familiar with the route before you ride it and download the gps file before you get to Elmore. This ride (NOT RACE) is held on open public roads, and therefore everyone is expected to be alert, ride with respect, and follow all the rules of the road. Please ride single file, there will be plenty of time to congregate at aid stations and back at the lake. We suggest that you use a flashing bike taillight if possible. Bottom line is that we want you all to be safe, have fun, and challenge yourselves. 

After the ride. Once you have completed the ride, you MUST check back in at the registration table. Here you will receive all of your post ride essentials like your meal, drink ticket and t-shirt. We have some delicious food and cold beverages waiting for you at the end! In order to cut down waste, we ask that people bring their own utensils and plates/bowls to eat with. In the event that you forget yours, we will have some compostable ones on hand. Drink tickets can be used at the beverage tent behind the store. If you are looking for more food or drink, The Elmore Store will have plenty of both on hand. There will be a community talent show starting at 1:00, followed by music starting at 3:00,  and then fireworks at dusk. All of this can be enjoyed from the back lawn and decks of The Elmore Store or floating in the lake. Bring your family and friends and make a day of it!

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: DROP THE HAMMER Progression
EventNotes:
Are you ready to Drop the Hammer?
It’s one of Bentonville’s must-hit features — and if you’re tired of just staring it down, this 2-day event is built for you. 2 days, 6 hours, one goal…check that box! We limit this session to SIX RIDERS, so one on one attention is abundant. Check out THIS video of the process. 

What to Expect:
Day 1 – 8AM - 11AM We’ll meet at Slaughter Pen and use both The Ride Series Ground School and the Purpose-Built Skills Park drops to dial in body position, timing, and technique — working progressively bigger throughout the session.

Day 2 – 8AM - 11AM We’ll start back at Slaughter Pen to sharpen up, then pedal over to Drop the Hammer to put it all together. After sending it, we’ll work on linking multiple drops with confidence and flow.

You’ll leave with:
Solid drop technique
The mindset to tackle intimidating features
The skills to keep progressing on your MTB journey

Is this for you? Well, only you can decide that…but we're gonna give you some guidelines ;) 

  • You're consistently hitting the largest intermediate drop at the Skills Park 

  • You're comfortable with the drops on Huntley Air Raid and Mad Hatter

  • You're ready to lock in both mentally and physically to check this one off! 

*This session requires full enrollment in order to proceed.

For more information, follow us on our Instagram page and hop on our website to learn more:  www.woznwa.com

 

Join us for This Month's Flagship Ride 

10:00am - 12:00pm
Meeting Location: 205 NE B St near Lawrence Plaza. Look for the WOZ Flags and tent. Don't forget to join us at the post-ride social starting at 12:00pm at Falfurrias at AC Hotel!

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. 

If you're new to mountain biking OR have never done a fundamentals skills clinic we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WOZ Fundamental Skills Clinic during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills course from one of our WOZ certified instructors will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

What do you need to attend the Flagship?  A mountain bike in good working order (contact a local bike shop for a tune up), helmet, closed toe athletic shoes, flat repair kit, water and snacks.  We also recommend sunglasses for eye protection and gloves.

***Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skills and endurance levels *** We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we’ve laid out a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, milage and proposed trails.  Being in the right group makes a better ride for all. 

At registration first choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Remember if you want to ride with a friend, register ASAP in the same Level AND Group # to ensure you'll be in the same group.  

Choose your group:

FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS CLINIC... this is the starting place
Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike,  it’s been a little longer than you would like to admit, OR you've never taken this clinic before….. Welcome!   You have to start somewhere and this is the place!  Even the most advanced riders need to brush up on these essential skills.  This Skills Clinic will cover the fundamental of mountain biking and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. 

Skill Level 1 

Skills you can perform:
Staying upright while pedaling
Fitness Level- no requirement 

GREEN ….New
You’ve ridden on the dirt multiple times now and you are starting to get the hang of things. You are now putting those skills from the clinic into play and working on shifting, braking, and body position.  Ride 5-7 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill level 1+
Level pedals while riding 
Riding with one finger over L & R brake levers
Getting to know berms (those are those turns with the dirt) 
Fitness Level 1 
Able to ride 30 minutes on easy terrain
Climbing a hill on the bike might require a breather break on the way up, and at the top of the hill. (I thought hills were for going down??)

GREEN +.... New with constant improvement 
Here to add the obstacles and steeper hills, but you are taking fewer breaks and pushing the ride time and mileage.  You are attempting more rocky surfaces, bridges and to roll over roots. (Yep we just roll right over those suckers.) Distances up to 8 miles or 2 hours are doable. Down Tristan’s?  Let go up it! Ride 5-7 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill level 2+
Standing on level pedals in “ready” position comfortably
Getting comfortable with appropriate gear shifting 
Novice on cornering and berms 
Comfortable crossing bridges 
Okay rolling over low roots/rocks and through tight trees  
Fitness Level Required 2 
You ride 2x a week
You can handle non-stop riding for up to an hour on easy terrain, after that it’s hit or miss.
You can climb up Crystal Bridges hill without stopping, but give me a breather at the top!

BLUE ....Confident and Fit.... attempting rock gardens
The rides are getting longer and the pace quicker.  Getting quicker out of berms you are confident in shifting, comfortable on single track and open to attempting obstacles.  You’re getting the hang of Coler, riding most of Slaughter Pen, and may have ridden Back 40 or at least parts of it. Ride 9-12 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill Level 3+
Controlled braking
Must be comfortable cornering and with berms 
Bike-body separation are natural
Comfortable with most moderate terrain (steeper, rockier, wetter, etc.)
Confident with wide switchbacks
Able to look up the trail and anticipate shifting, position change, obstacles, etc.
Fitness Level 3 
You ride 2-3x a week on an average in season week
You can climb longer with soft pedaling as a recovery instead of stopping
You can ride moderate pace for 2 hours with minimal stops 
Must be able to climb Ozone 
Intermediate skill group: here because you’re still working on upping the mileage and ride time. 15 miles or 3 hours might be my cutoff!                 
                              
BLUE +... Confident, fit and ready for a 3hr ride
You’ve been riding for awhile now, put a lot of time and mileage in to riding confidently and tackling bigger challenges are a regular thing. You are comfortable with fast descents, rock gardens, more technical climbs and features.  Ride 10-15 miles. 
Skills you can perform: 
Skill Level 4+ Confident with bike handling skills with roots, rocks, tight corners, etc
Your tires are leaving the ground
Climbing technical terrain 
Comfortable in tight Berms/Switchbacks and exit with acceleration 
Can ride technical single track 
Able to get up and over moderate obstacles up to 6 inches off ground
Fitness Level 4 
Riding 3-4x a week 
3  hour rides are doable
Able to climb continuously without breaks 
Can ride most of Back 40 

BLACK....Advanced rider and can ride with a pro-mtb'r
Ride now, talk later.  You are up for fast paced, intense, challenging, demanding, some good ol light-hearted competition!  Be ready to ride fast, nail some jumps and drops, and possibly get a QOM in the meantime! Ride 15+ miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill Level 5+
Comfortable with drops and changing technical terrain 
Hop over obstacles  
Able to perform front wheel/rear wheel lifts (up to 6 inches as needed) 
Fitness Level 5  
Riding 4-5x a week 
Considers racing around the Back 40 in around 3hrs FUN
Ready to move at a rapid pace throughout ride
Continuous movement, breaks only to refuel 
Can ride Rock Solid and Schroen Train

EventNotes:
Sloppy Jon’s 2026

Sloppy Jon’s is a community-focused, mixed-surface ride hosted by It’s Just A Hill. This is not a race. There is no podium. It is a social ride built around challenging routes, good company, and bringing people together through bikes.

Start Location (New for 2026)

Sloppy Jon’s will start and finish at the Woody Lowden Recreation Center in Foster, RI.

After three years of rolling out from Jon’s house, the event is taking a small step forward and using a proper start location. This gives us more space, better parking, and a smoother day for everyone while keeping the same community-first feel.

Please respect the recreation center, property, and neighbors. We want to be invited back.

Registration & Capacity

Sloppy Jon’s is a free event. We do not want money to be a barrier to entry or participation.

Registration is limited to 150 riders. Please only sign up if you genuinely plan to attend. If your plans change, we ask that you withdraw your registration so someone on the waitlist can take your spot.

A waitlist will be enabled once the event fills. If space opens up, riders will be admitted in the order they joined the waitlist. We appreciate everyone helping keep this fair and accessible for the whole community.

Routes & Support

Sloppy Jon's 2026 features five route options, including three gravel and two paved.

Gravel Routes (Mixed Surface)
We encourage a gravel bike with some extra tire clearance, but you can ride any type of bike you'd like.

Extra Sloppy / 100 Miles / 39% paved (Strava)
Standard Slop / 69 Miles / 44% paved (Strava)
Little Sloppy / 44 Miles / 42% paved (Strava)

Most of the gravel is relatively smooth with a couple of bony sections mixed in. All gravel routes pass Oneco Market and the IJAH x NBX rest stop, with hydration and snacks provided at the latter.

Paved Routes
No Slop Century / 100 Miles
No Slop Metric / 100km

Support
This is a mostly self-supported ride. Riders are responsible for navigation, hydration, nutrition, and mechanical support. All routes include opportunities to stop at convenience stores along the way. Route changes will be allowed prior to the event, pending availability.

Event Support

Putting Sloppy Jon’s together does come with real costs. Renting the race center, providing ride snacks, and covering basic logistics all add up. We believe the time and money spent are worth it for the local cycling community, and optional donations help make that possible.

If you are able to contribute, thank you. If not, no problem at all. Show up, ride your bike, and be part of it.

Post-Ride

After the ride, everyone is invited to stick around for a post-ride potluck, featuring signature Sloppy Joe sandwiches and dirt cups for dessert.

Event Details

Routes, timing, and final details will be shared closer to the event date via Strava and the It’s Just A Hill channels.

EventNotes:
Welcome to The Battle Of Toledo!

NOMBS, The Black Swamp Riders, The Right Direction, and City Of Toledo Parks are inviting YOU to come defend your home states honor in this race! We are right on the Michigan border, and we are welcoming the Michigan riders to come down and race! Let's see which state takes home the most podiums!

THIS EVENT IS RAIN OR SHINE!

Course Info

The Jermain Ottawa trail in downtown Toledo is often overlooked, but truly a great trail created and maintained by volunteer efforts. This will be a FAST course, but there are some unique challenges using this trail for a race course. There is a section where the trail passes under a bridge that is narrow. To mitigate risks of two way race traffic on this narrow section we are adding a cyclocross inspired course feature under the bridge. This narrow section will require racers to dismount and run the short section under the bridge, with no passing allowed in the run section. There will be dismount and remount points marked, and course marshals at each run section. Racers must dismount before the markers and will be assessed a time penalty if course marshals observe a violation. Is this unusual for a MTB race? Yup, sure is, but this is a great solution that will make these sections safer and add an interesting challenge to your race! Start practicing those dismounts now!

10am Jr. Novice course notes:

  • Approximately 5 mile lap.
  • Approximately 125' elevation.
  • No dismount section.
  • Jr's get 2 laps, 30 minute cutoff to start lap 2.
  • Scored on laps completed.

Noon race:

  • Approximately 6.5 mile lap.
  • 188' elevation.
  • Lap counts:
    • E-bike, 2 laps
    • Cat1, 3 laps
    • Cat2, 2 laps
    • Cat3, 1 lap
  • 1 road crossing per lap, road is closed.
  • 1 dismount section in each lap to accommodate 2 way traffic under a bridge. You run it both ways, time penalty if you don't.

Course on Trail Forks.

Camping at the race:

The City OF Toledo Parks Dept. is graciously allowing a limited amount of car camping at the race venue, with the following rules:

  • Limited to 20 cars/vans/small trailers.
  • Brand new flush toilets!
  • No fires!

Day Of Registration:

While we strongly encourage you to preregister (and greatly appreciate you doing so as it helps the event go more smoothly), there will be "day of" registration. It will be an extra $10 after 6pm Saturday evening, and will close at 10am.

 

Race day Schedule:

  • 9am registration/packet pickup opens
  • 9:30am Cat 3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race day of registration closes
  • 10am Cat3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race start
  • 10am day of registration & number pickup closes.
  • 11:40 am Jr Novice podiums and riders Meeting
  • 12pm Cat 1 & E-Bike categories start
  • 12:40pm All remaining cat 2 and cat 3 categories start. THIS TIME IS APPROXIMATE!
  • 2:30-3pm podiums.
  • Adaptive racers, we may alter where in the schedule you start as we work with you and learn what works best. 

!!!!!!!Start time notes!!!!!

In an effort to offer a safer and more fun race environment for all participants we are now starting Cat 2 and Cat 3 racers after Cat 1 and E Bikes have completed one lap. This greatly reduces conflict between very fast cat 1 and E Bike racers passing novice racers by nearly eliminating lap traffic. The posted start time of 12:40m for cat 2 & 3 is approximate. We will begin releasing the remaining cat 2 & 3 waves after Cat 1 racers go through scoring. Know your wave number!

10am Cat3 Jr. Novice Races

You may have noticed that we are doing Cat3 Jr novice races early in the day and be asking "hey, what's up with that?" We want to give Jr's, and particularly novice Jr's the best race day experience we can. Separating the Jr. novice races to an earlier start allows us to do 3 things:

  • Fewer racers on course for the race.
  • For families where the one or both parents also race it gives the parents a chance to spectate and cheer their kids.
  • Novice Jr's get their own start, with more people cheering and spectating. Bring the cowbells!

USA Cycling Licenses, and NOMBS Series Championship rules & eligibility:

NOMBS is proud to be bringing a USAC sanctioned series to Ohio and be hosting the official USA Cycling Ohio MTB Championship. Partnering with USA Cycling helps us offer you a great series with structure, consistent categories & scoring, good insurance for landowners, and allows an opportunity for riders with goals outside Ohio to earn USAC points. 

USA Cycling Race Age:

 Your “race age” is the age you will be on December 31st. This rule exists so that a person does not have to change the age group they are entering partway through a race season. 

NOMBS Series Championship Eligibility rules:

  1. A rider must have a current USA Cycling License (need not reside in Ohio).
  2. Scored on best 5 races.
  3. In the event of a points tie the season final race is the tie breaker.
  4. Season Finale is double points.

Complete series rules can be found here.

This is the 33rd year of the oldest ongoing gravel race in the Midwest!!!

It takes place in Iowa's driftless region and has views that'll take your breath away.  

This year we decided to do an old school throwback race and do a shotgun start for only 1 route.  We're only offering the 40 mile route.  Yes the route includes level B & C roads.    Remember, the Level C roads are private property and are NOT allowed to be ridden, except for on race day.

Count on roughly 1,000 ft of climb per 10 miles but you won't notice because you'll be so busy enjoying the beautiful countryside.

The route will be uploaded prior to the race so watch for that.  Will the route be marked?  Since there's only 1 distance, the chance is good.   Now does that mean you can solely rely on the markings?   No, you should follow the Ride2 With GPS you download.

There will be an aid station around mile 20.  Outside aid is NOT permitted.  This aid station will be a mandatory check point as well.

Check-in and bib pick are TBD. 

What surprises do I have in store this year?  Great question but the answer is, you'll have to wait to see.  

Will there be music and an awards ceremony?  YES!!!

Rules: Helmets are required.  No Karen's, Richards, or Kooks.  No support vehicles or outside support.  I don't want to see random vehicles out on the routes meeting racers.  Aid stations are for volunteers and racers only. Please. 

Chuck Norris would say, "don't forget to bring your legs, your friend's legs, your neighbor's legs, actually just bring all the legs there are.

    • “The Bad” If you've been riding gravel events for awhile,  finished last year's ride and were up for more, “The bad” is a tough +/-55 miles with +/-6,000' elevation, should be enough to have most riders seeing cross eyed and wishing they'd opted for a shorter route.
    • “The ugly” This +/-70 mile loop with +/-8,000' of elevation monster…. is savage. It will also be restricted to a field of 30 riders, and will have a time cut off at the first time through the feed zone.
    • "Type 1 fun" A mostly paved ride with a few miles of maintained gravel road. 24 miles, 2,500" elevation. Suitable for a confident rider on 30mm tires.
  • A staffed feed stop for all ride options. This stop will be stocked with Orchard Hill Breadworks baked goods, water, drink mix, fruit, and maple syrup shots!
  • Post ride pizza and dessert for all riders. (Eat up, we're not counting how many slices you take)
  • Want to bring the family and enjoy an early fall day with bikes and wood fired pizza? Sign up for “Just pizza” and we'll gladly share some family friendly shorter loops suitable for all ability levels. 

The Courses are SELF NAVIGATED.  We like arrows, but we share these roads and trails with a wide variety of users.  It has become apparent that not all non-bikers share that like!  Conclusion: no arrows are better than wrong arrows!  The GPS track and cue sheets will be emailed a day or two before the event as well.  

Everyone riding the Dirty Pizza is strongly encouraged to ride with a navigation device (links shared 3 days prior to event).  Cue sheets will also be available.  

To some, the most important feature of the day is the Post Ride Feed where you will be treated to Noah's wood oven fired pizza feast back at the Orchard Hill Pavillion.

WHAT TO BRING…

  • Good, Bad and Ugly will all best be tackled on 42mm or larger tires.
  • Type 1 fun can be ridden on a narrower tire, but you'll still be happy riding a cushy 42mm gravel set up.
  • This ride is self supported. Bring your own gear to change flats and make minor repairs.
  • Sag support will be available "On Call", but in some sections of the course that will mean walking a bit to get cell reception and or access to a road.
  • The pizza feast will consist of wood fired pizza with a variety of toppings. Gluten free crusts available.
  • BYOB
  • See more about the venue: www.orchardhillbreadworks.com

Call or email if you have questions: 603-835-7845, noah@orchardhillbreadworks.com

Your registration fee benefits The Salvation Army's Pathway of Hope program. EventName: 2026 RI North South Trail Gravel Race/ Ride
EventNotes:
Important Note:  Parking for the Start is ½ mile up Wallum Lake Road at the 1st Dirt Trail Head because the main entrance to the Park doesn't open until after 8 AM, you would need to pay to park, and the line to enter the park is long.

This is the FREE Labor Day  ”Reach the Beach” NS Trail Gravel Race/Ride.  The Start will be at the trail head parking in Douglas, MA.  All gravel segments will be New Strava segments with entrants times posting after the race.  Awards will be given for winners for the OA finish in each catagory.   This is a FREE Event and all we ask is that all participants make a Tax deductible donation to the “Tunnels to Towers” organization www.t2t.org that supports Our Veterans and First Responders. Or you can make a donation to the Whitin Community Center www.whitincommunitycenter.com.  This is a completely Non-Profit event to give back to those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our FREEDOM!

The GPS track is provided.  It follows the entire NS trail from Douglas, MA 82 miles  to Blue Shutters Beach in Charlestown, RI.  The Buck Hill section of the NS Trail is “by passed” because it’s unridable.  Everything on the Track can be ridden by a skilled rider.  There is a mix of road, gravel, cart roads, single track and some short “hike a bike” sections.   Any bike Gravel or Mountain Bike with no wider than 2.1 tires will be a good choice to best manage the course.  The woods do have deer flys so, bring bug repellent.

The best plan is to have your Family spend the day  at Blue Shutters Beach in Charlestown, RI where the ride Finishes.   Changing and shower facilities are available at the Beach.   You do need to pay for a day beach pass but, after 5 PM entry is free.   I anticipate a finish around 4 PM.

Pre Registration Only,  No Race Day Entries

EventName: Pineapple Crush Cross - PACX Series Race #1
EventNotes:
Hello Cyclocross Community! 

It is our 5-year anniversary. Come celebrate with us! There will be more of everything, more prizes, more cash, more pineapples and more FUN! Join the crew of Pineapple Crush Cross as we again "takeover" the prestigious Fifth Street 'Cross course to bring you “The Pineapple Cruuush”.

This year we are trying something new, guaranteed to add an additional twist to racing (as if this course needed another twist, right?)  This year we will be awarding each category a fastest lap preme and fastest timed section preme. Here’s the twist, you won’t know what lap we are counting until you line up! Timed section will be identified beforehand so you can practice.

To add to the fun, one of last year’s omnium winners has donated their winnings back to the race in the form of a first lap preme for all the junior and U18 fields! Thanks Sarah!!

We will have the relay race again sponsored by PT Bike Fit. See below for more details on the relay race and how to sign up.

Thanks to Fifth Street Cross and the Emmaus Compost Center for creating and hosting this course. Fifth Street Cross, PA’s premier weeknight cyclocross and cross country race course starts Thursday 9/3 for those who want a preview. At our race you will find the widest range of features and obstacles including off camber, sweeping and hairpin turns, steps, barriers, pump track section and the crush ‘em like a pineapple Shimano Hill. You will definitely "bust the rust" on ALL your 'cross skills and have the most fun doing it! Whatever the weather, you are guaranteed to have a great time racing ‘cross. And we highly encourage dancing to DJ Big Daddy Blake’s awesome tunes!

Here’s all the details, hope to see you there!

Your Pineapple Crush Crew,

Mel, Jen & Josh (and our amazing crew of volunteers, you know who you are!)

PARKING: Only permitted outside the gates of the Compost Center. We have two places for you to park. 

1.      Klines Lane Parking Lot, 101 Klines Ln, Emmaus, PA 18049. Located next to the Compost Center entrance road. There are also a few spots at the entrance, but space is very limited.

2.      Seventh Generations Charter School; parking entrances on Minor St. and also Klines Ln. Located across the street from the Compost Center.

To get to the course from the corner of Klines Ln and Minor St, you will follow the access road Robert Rodale Way past the gates. The course, porto potties, and registration are all inside the gates.

REGISTRATION: Opens at 7:30 am and closes 30 minutes prior to the start of each race. Same day registration will be available for $10 on top of the standard rate. Additional races are $10 each and that discount is applied automatically during checkout in Bikereg. No discount code needed. Racing age is determined by your age on December 31, 2027.

CALL UPS: Update: First row will be according to last year’s PACX series standings, with first call up to the winner of that category.  Then will be according to your current standings in Cross Results and then order of signup. www.crossresults.com. Last year's PACX winner will get first call up if racing in the category they won in.

LITTLE BELGIANS FUN RACE: Our youngest racers are welcome to test out their legs and cornering skills by doing a few laps of the mini course set up in the soccer field. Exact location TBD pending soccer game schedule. The Little Belgium's race will start at 12:30 PM and racers will do 2-3 laps. This is a very simple course suitable for little ones.

TEAM TENTS: We have space for about (10) team tents in the parking lot and around the course. Sign up is in registration and is first come first serve. Team tents and gear will need to be walked/rolled/hand trucked into the Compost Center.

PT Bike Fit RELAY RACE: Inspired by the World Championships relay race, we bring you our very own tropical fruit inspired relay race. Our goal with the relay is to promote greater ‘cross community collaboration and bring together different categories of racers, or entire families, who would not normally be racing together. The relay is FREE we just need one person to sign up and pick a team name.

If you would like participate, please follow these steps.

1.      Recruit your team or register solo-looking for a team. Teams must consist of (4) riders and at least (1) Masters and (1) Junior the rest of the team is up to you!

2.      Team leaders can register FREE for the relay.

3.      Let us know what your Team Name is!

4.      Solo registrants will be teamed ad hoc

5.      Figure out your strategy, what will your line up be?

PREMES:

·      Each category will be awarded a $25 fastest lap preme. Timed lap will be shared prior to the start of the race.

·      Each category will be awarded a $15 fasted timed section preme. Timed section will be identified with course markings during preride.

·      Each Junior race and U18 race category will be awarded a first lap preme. Junior race will receive $25 and U18 $40.

FREE ENTRY: Thanks to PA Cycling Association all Junior and U20 racers are FREE entry. If your youth would like to race in a different field, please use code PineappleJunior for free registration.

  • UNDRBUDR for sponsoring the Elite Race races cash and podium prizes!

  • PA Cycling Association for sponsoring Junior and U20 FREE registration and prizes!

  • PT Bike Fit for sponsoring the relay and podium prizes!

  • New Trail Brewing for the podium beers!

  • Stans for the podium prizes!

  • Sock Guy and GoCycling for podium prizes! Pineapple Socks!

WINNEWANA from York Food & Drink is a self-supported mixed terrain ride. The ride is NOT A RACE and it’s NOT A NO DROP RIDE either. You could call it a glorified training ride if you really need to call it something. You can go as fast or as slow as you'd like... just come ride your bike and have a good time. Really... It's that simple.

RIDER'S GUIDE - The guide will be sent out on Friday after registration closes to all who have registered. The rider's guide will have the finalized routes and all the info you need to have a good time!

DATE - Sunday, September 6th, 2026

LOCATION - York Food & Drink - 1928 Packard St, Ann Arbor, MI 48104

TIME - 100-mile @ 7:11am. 100k @ 9:11am. 50k @ 10:11am

3 FLAVORS - There will be 3 flavors available to enjoy. 50k, 100k, and 100-miles. Sign up for whatever one you think you'll do and then on the day of the event you can switch if you'd like. 50k is for people looking to get a taste of gravel riding or to enjoy a super chill ride. 100k is for the seasoned rider looking to get in a good workout with friends. The 100-miler is for the hard core gravel enthusiast and it gets a little spicy towards the end.

ROUTE - The route is on OPEN ROADS. Riders must obey all traffic laws, including stopping at STOP signs, not crossing the center line of the road, etc. The routes will NOT be marked and you will have to upload the route to your Garmin. These routes will be included in the rider's guide that will be sent out closer to the ride.

STICKERS - Produced by Dexter Graphic Arts and provided by Ann Arbor Velo Club and will be available after the ride.

PHOTOS - Matthew Orwig Photography will be taking photos at various points on the courses. Photos will be available within a few days of the event.

POST-RIDE - There will be beverages and food available for purchase.

RIDE LOCAL - Thank you to York Food & Drink, Ann Arbor Velo Club for supporting the local cycling community and for helping to make this ride possible. Please continue to support the local businesses that support you, so cool shit like this can happen for years to come! If you enjoyed yourself at this ride, please join us for some of our other rad rides - BLØM, THE PLEASANT LAKE RIDE, THE WATERMOO, and WINNEWANA.

Cyclocross Race Training at Hale Education. 

Cyclocross (often abbreviated CX or simply “cross”) is a multi-terrain bicycle racing discipline that combines the speed of road cycling, the technical challenges of mountain biking, and the obstacles and barriers of a steeplechase. At Hale, we have fields, stairs, gravel, a sandpit, and a beach to ride, with fewer rocks and roots than many of Hale's other trails. You can expect two twenty-minute heats and a multiple-lap course.  

Driving Directions: Hale’s South Entrance – next to 573 Dover Road, Westwood, MA, 02090 

Support MTB at Hale 

Mountain bikers of all ages are drawn to Hale’s rugged, varied terrain just miles from Boston’s city line, and we’ve been eagerly expanding youth mountain biking program over the past five years. 

Hale MTB Camp focuses on skill-building and ride time for an existing community of young mountain bikers. Youth MTB Club is growing that community through a fantastic team of volunteer coaches who coordinate recreational rides and opportunities to participate in races and events throughout New England. Intrepid Academy at Hale students also enjoy time on the trails as part of their semester at Hale. 

We’re thrilled with our progress and are helping hundreds of riders advance, but with your help, we can do more. 

Thank you for supporting MTB opportunities for youth by making your donation today. 

About Hale 

Hale is a nonprofit organization that serves nearly 16,000 people annually. We count on donations from people like you to help us provide an outdoor experience to the children in Greater Boston. Your gift today will help us continue to run great programs like this one, steward the land for our community, and ensure Greater Boston’s kids have transformational camp experiences. 

By registering for Hale’s events and programs, you consent to its privacy policy, media policy, and refund policies.

EventName: Island Cat ~ Wedding on the Water
EventNotes:
Madeline Island Alley Cat Rider Info
#weddingcat ~ Wedding on the Water
September 11th-13th 2026

Year 5 of Island Cat is bringing you a love story. Evan & I met after I moved to the island, became friends and then during year 2 of Island Cat he met all my pals, the folks that know me best and our friendship blossomed into riding this wonderful wave of life together. We want to celebrate our people the most! 

How to get to the island:
Madeline Island Ferry Line boats run every half hour from 10a-6p with a few later evening drops from Bayfield, WI to Island 9 & 10pm (last boat Friday only). This is a 2.5 mile and 25 min ride. All vehicles are allowed and tickets are first come first served. Visit www.madferry.com as this schedule may change.

Provisions to bring:
Weekend entry fee: 1 pack of hot dogs, veggie dog or alt. I’m supplying all the buns.  
Pack like you would to tent camp, bring food & any gear you may need. Camp chairs! Plate, bowl, utensils, reusable cafe cup, etc. Darlings Grocery is open 7 days a week 10a-6p. There are a few restaurants on the island too. Bring cash for the main race and afterparty at Tom’s. Bike lights, helmets, & locks are required. Swim gear if the temps are still nice we dip. Inclement weather has been known to happen in Lake Superior, be advised.

Parking:
Public restrooms & free overnight parking is located at 868 Whitefish St, Bayfield, WI 54814 known as the “public lot”.
Please set up camp, drive with your bike to park here as there is not a lot of parking at the property for non-adventure vehicles. 

Camping at the South Shore House:
South Shore House
This year we are setting up camp on our 5 acre new-to-us property! The fire number is 320 Big Arns Rd. but all campers will enter the driveway from South Shore Rd. across from Islewood Rd. and follow the camp signs & volunteers to your camp pads. If you are tent camping unload and then park in the public parking lot downtown and use a bike for the weekend. Tent space and some room for van setups are available. Please contact me to reserve space if you need to van camp.
Biff’s for restrooms, potable water, no electric hook ups. Please no dogs as our ducks are free range.

There are public showers for a $2 fee at Tom’s Burned Down Cafe.

Camping is free, please be respectful. This is our home, you better pack-in pack-out.

Riders are responsible for all meals.

Friday 9/11
Arrival times can vary so set up camp and go explore!
5p -Introductions, weekend overview & safety meeting.
6p -Capser Capsized Gravel Criterium time launches before sunset (4 laps critty cross style). Starting located at Capser West Trailhead across from Freak Farm (bring lights, helmet, bug spray, extra layers). We will group ride to the start. 

Evan & I are having an open house & bonfire Friday eve from 6-8p. Roller dog cart, cocktail camper by The Briar and Hot Island Sauna’s new camper sauna to name a few treats for the night.

Saturday 9/12
9a - 12p ~ Evan & Lilah’s Wedding on the Water  (ceremony space was limited and Island Cat’s afterparty is our wedding afterparty too! So we will all celebrate together after your race.)
1:30p -Manifests drop @ Tom’s Burned Down Cafe here

Sunday 9/7
Departure day?? But it actually doesn't have to be. Welcome to camp till Monday!
For all the pals that want to stay we will find a beach to hang at and go for a group ride as well. 

Safe Space Policy:
Any unsafe behavior, verbal abuse and violent actions will immediately remove you from the premise of any private property or business affiliated with this event.

Ride Rules:
You must wear a helmet and have lights. Obey all traffic right of way. 

It’s just an alley cat, don’t be so serious :)

*Gichigami Productions is not responsible for any incidents. In the event of an emergency dial 911 and EMS will transport to Ashland Tamarack. Contact Lilah Guertin at 715-209-2022 with any accidents/injuries directly after EMS is called. Use the buddy system, it's an island.

John Brown Time Trial Series

Growin the Sport while Racin 4 Peanuts –Thursday’s 6/11, 7/23, 8/20, & 9/10

 

INFO: The John Brown Time Trial Series – Where growin the sport and racin 4 peanuts collide.  The John Brown Time Trial Emporium has something for everyone. If you need us to invent a category we will just for you. Getting on your bike, going fast and making friend is what grows the sport. Don’t be fooled, the best athletes in the Midwest will grace this race with their best carbon aero tuck and retro fixie with wool jersey.

This is your chance to finally see if your TT bike is that much faster than your road bike. Or race a solo race and then do a “duo” with your friend. Try the coed “duo” to! Do you feel better your second race? Then your need a harder warm up for future events.

COURSE: The fastest and flattest 5-mile course in Kansas! This predominately West to East course follows the Kansas river bottoms road Northwest of DeSoto. See if you can join the “9-minute club!” for men or “10-minute club!” for women.

REGISTRATION: Registration is after 5:45pm and work with us since we are all hustling here after our day jobs. Race starts after 6:30pm Race entry is $25 and you get to race two 5-mile TT’s. During the longer summer months, a 3rd race may be possible if you are a sicko!  There are no bathrooms so take care of biz on the way in. 

NOTES: Race intervals will be 30 to 60 seconds and will be determine by number of racers signed up. After the first wave goes we’ll take a 5 to 10-minute break and let you change gear and bikes to race your second time trial of the evening. You don’t have to race twice, but there is no charge. During the height of the summer we may allow a limited number of riders to race three 5 mile TT’s.

CATEGORIES: Men, Open, Cat 4, Cat 5, Masters 40+, 50+, & 60+  Women, Open, Cat 4, Masters 40+, 50+, & 60+

1st Timer Category (1st USAC race ever), Tri Category (holds USAT license and never raced USAC)

RACE TYPES:

Aero – Use everything that is USA Cycling legal! Shave your arms and eye brows too!

Modern Merckx – no aero gear, but aero “road” frames allowed. Like Venge, and Madone. Wheels up to 30 mm deep allowed.

Retro Merckx – no aero road bike tubing, round tubes only. Box rims. 5-second bonus for Wool Jersey

Single Speed – Retro Merckx plus only ONE gear, fixed or single. Must have working front break.

Duo – 2 People, time taken off 2nd rider. May combine other race types. Like Merckx or Aero Duo.

Duo (coed) – Male/female, time taken off 2nd rider.

Cheater Class – something that doesn’t fit the above categories.

Promoter reserves right to qualify bikes and equipment for each race. No cheaters allowed, except in Cheater Class.

PRIZES:

You are racing 4 peanuts, but we’ll give first in every category a Revolution Racing Pint glass, that we may randomly fill up. End of season beer party! We’ll make up some series placings as the year goes on, but officially the only prize is the pint glass after each day of racing.

EventNotes:
The Pisgah Monster-Cross Challenge is the premiere all-road racing event in the region. Participants are challenged to complete a 69.2 mile course with 8,777’of climbing along scenic gravel and paved roads. The riders will be treated to some of the finest gravel roads in the Pisgah and Nantahala National Forests, which is a one-of-a-kind opportunity in the racing world. Monster-Cross is a dream gravel endurance event where keen race tactics and strategy, along with overall fitness, proper gear selection, and sheer luck are key to success. 

There will be three Rest Areas along the way that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks,  bars), first aid, and neutral mechanical support. Racers will be covering a lot of ground on the map, riding through some of the most quintessential Pisgah forest, not without brutal terrain and breathtaking scenery.
